sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: If you're standing on the sidewalk in the New York Financial District,
sentences.zh: 如果你站在纽约金融区的街道上，

sentences.en: in the shadows of glass skyscrapers,
sentences.zh: 在玻璃摩天大楼的阴影下，

sentences.en: you definitely don't feel like you're at the seaside.
sentences.zh: 你绝对不会觉得这里是海边。

sentences.en: But head a few blocks south, and suddenly you're at the edge of the continent,
sentences.zh: 但往南走几个街区，你突然就到了大陆的边缘，

sentences.en: looking out at the water.
sentences.zh: 眺望着水面。

sentences.en: That's producer Emmett Fitzgerald.
sentences.zh: 那是制片人埃米特·菲茨杰拉德。

sentences.en: There are docks and seagulls, and ferry boats ready to take you island hopping.
sentences.zh: 那里有码头、海鸥，还有准备带你跳岛游的渡轮。

sentences.en: Writer Paul Greenberg moved into an apartment down here over a decade ago.
sentences.zh: 作家保罗·格林伯格十多年前搬到了这附近的公寓。

sentences.en: And up until that point, like a lot of New Yorkers,
sentences.zh: 在那之前，像许多纽约人一样，

sentences.en: I didn't really pay that much attention to the sea.
sentences.zh: 我并没有太关注大海。

sentences.en: If I wanted to go to the ocean, I would go to Martha's Vineyard or Long Island.
sentences.zh: 如果我想去海边，我会去玛莎葡萄园岛或长岛。

sentences.en: But then he started noticing all these maritime buildings,
sentences.zh: 但后来他开始注意到所有这些海事建筑，

sentences.en: like the old Fulton Fish Market, where fishermen used to sell their catch to restaurants.
sentences.zh: 比如旧富尔顿鱼市场，渔民们过去常在那里把捕获的海鲜卖给餐馆。

sentences.en: I suddenly was sort of confronted with the fact that New York, Manhattan,
sentences.zh: 我突然意识到一个事实：纽约，曼哈顿，

sentences.en: is really a very ocean-y kind of place.
sentences.zh: 其实是一个非常有海洋气息的地方。

sentences.en: Greenberg actually writes about the ocean for a living.
sentences.zh: 格林伯格实际上是以写海洋为生的。

sentences.en: His most recent book is called American Catch.
sentences.zh: 他最近的一本书叫《美国渔获》。

sentences.en: And he started to research the relationship between New York City and the sea.
sentences.zh: 他开始研究纽约市与海洋之间的关系。

sentences.en: But then, in 2012, something happened that made that relationship impossible to ignore.
sentences.zh: 但后来，在2012年，发生了一件事，让这种关系变得无法忽视。

sentences.en: Hurricane Sandy crashing on shore.
sentences.zh: 飓风“桑迪”席卷海岸。

sentences.en: Winds now at 90 miles per hour.
sentences.zh: 风速现已达到每小时90英里。

sentences.en: And this storm is so big, so vast, 60 million Americans will feel its power.
sentences.zh: 这场风暴如此巨大、如此广阔，6000万美国人将感受到它的威力。

sentences.en: Just south of the South Street Seabour, take a look out here.
sentences.zh: 就在南街海港以南，往这边看。

sentences.en: That is the Brooklyn Bridge.
sentences.zh: 那是布鲁克林大桥。

sentences.en: And look at how those winds are whipping the river around.
sentences.zh: 看看那些风是如何搅动河水的。

sentences.en: Hurricane Sandy's storm surge inundated neighborhoods throughout New York City.
sentences.zh: 飓风“桑迪”的风暴潮淹没了纽约市各地的社区。

sentences.en: Seawater poured into the streets, flooding out apartment buildings and filling the subway tunnels.
sentences.zh: 海水涌入街道，淹没了公寓楼，灌满了地铁隧道。

sentences.en: Greenberg and his family waited out the storm in their 10th-floor apartment.
sentences.zh: 格林伯格和他的家人在他们10楼的公寓里躲避风暴。

sentences.en: We sat there and the storm hit and things started to rock and roll.
sentences.zh: 我们坐在那里，风暴袭来，东西开始摇晃。

sentences.en: And then everything went black.
sentences.zh: 然后一切都陷入了黑暗。

sentences.en: Sandy knocked out power across lower Manhattan.
sentences.zh: “桑迪”切断了曼哈顿下城的电力。

sentences.en: The day after, I immediately wanted to get a sense of what it was like.
sentences.zh: 第二天，我立刻想去看看情况如何。

sentences.en: So he walked down to the waterfront, past a bunch of bars and restaurants.
sentences.zh: 于是他走到海滨，经过了一堆酒吧和餐馆。

sentences.en: And when you peered in the windows, it looked as if there had been a horrible bar fight.
sentences.zh: 当你透过窗户往里看时，看起来就像发生了一场可怕的酒吧斗殴。

sentences.en: Because the water had come in, flooded up to eight or nine feet, and thrown all the chairs and tables up in the air.
sentences.zh: 因为水涌了进来，淹到了八九英尺高，把所有的椅子和桌子都抛到了空中。

sentences.en: But as he surveyed the damage, Greenberg also started to notice things about his neighborhood that he never had before.
sentences.zh: 但在他查看损失时，格林伯格也开始注意到他社区里以前从未注意到的事情。

sentences.en: Turns out that Broadway, and I live on Broadway, is a ridgeline.
sentences.zh: 原来百老汇——我就住在百老汇——是一条山脊线。

sentences.en: It's the high point between east and weSt.
sentences.zh: 它是东西方之间的高点。

sentences.en: And when Hurricane Sandy hit lower Manhattan, it got safer and safer and drier and drier the closer you were up to Broadway.
sentences.zh: 当飓风“桑迪”袭击曼哈顿下城时，你离百老汇越近，就越安全、越干燥。

sentences.en: He says the storm forced New Yorkers to see the relationship between their city and the ocean in a much more intimate way.
sentences.zh: 他说，这场风暴迫使纽约人以一种更亲密的方式看待他们的城市与海洋之间的关系。

sentences.en: Nothing acquaints you with your city's topography like living in the eye of a hurricane.
sentences.zh: 没有什么比生活在飓风眼中更能让你了解你所在城市的地形了。

sentences.en: And feeling that water flow up and rise up and literally start to swallow the city.
sentences.zh: 感受那水流涌上来、升起来，简直要吞噬这座城市。

sentences.en: Sandy took the lives of over 100 people in the United States and caused upwards of $50 billion in damage.
sentences.zh: “桑迪”在美国夺去了100多人的生命，造成了超过500亿美元的损失。

sentences.en: It was the second most expensive storm in U.S.
sentences.zh: 这是美国历史上

sentences.en: history.
sentences.zh: 第二昂贵的风暴。

sentences.en: And part of the reason why the storm was so destructive has to do with climate change.
sentences.zh: 风暴之所以如此具有破坏力，部分原因与气候变化有关。

sentences.en: Scientists have calculated that because of sea level rise driven by climate change,
sentences.zh: 科学家们计算出，由于气候变化导致的海平面上升，

sentences.en: Sandy flooded an additional 27 square miles and affected 83,000 more people than it would have otherwise.
sentences.zh: “桑迪”淹没了额外的27平方英里土地，影响了比预期多83000人。

sentences.en: There is a wake-up call here, and there is a lesson to be learned.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个警钟，也有一个教训需要吸取。

sentences.en: This is Governor Andrew Cuomo speaking in the storm's aftermath.
sentences.zh: 这是安德鲁·科莫州长在风暴过后的讲话。

sentences.en: There is a reality that has existed for a long time that we have been blind to.
sentences.zh: 有一个长期存在但我们一直视而不见的现实。

sentences.en: And that is climate change, extreme weather, call it what you will, and our vulnerability to it.
sentences.zh: 那就是气候变化、极端天气，随你怎么称呼它，以及我们对它的脆弱性。

sentences.en: It's undeniable, but that the frequency of extreme weather conditions is up.
sentences.zh: 这是不可否认的，极端天气条件的频率正在上升。

sentences.en: So it's going to be a rethinking, redesign of how we protect this metropolitan area from this increased frequency.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们将重新思考、重新设计如何保护这个大都市区免受这种日益频繁的灾害。

sentences.en: Architects and engineers are looking at different ways that cities like New York can redesign their infrastructure
sentences.zh: 建筑师和工程师正在研究不同的方法，让纽约这样的城市重新设计其基础设施，

sentences.en: to prepare for more extreme storm surges.
sentences.zh: 以应对更极端的风暴潮。

sentences.en: There's talk of floodgates and massive seawalls that would stretch across the entire harbor.
sentences.zh: 有人在谈论防洪闸和横跨整个港口的巨大海堤。

sentences.en: But Paul Greenberg says that one of the solutions for New York's future might lie in its paSt.
sentences.zh: 但保罗·格林伯格说，纽约未来的解决方案之一可能在于它的过去。

sentences.en: Well, so New York, in its natural state, was set up to deal with big storMs.
sentences.zh: 嗯，纽约在自然状态下，是能够应对大风暴的。

sentences.en: New York was built at the mouth of the Hudson River,
sentences.zh: 纽约建在哈德逊河口，

sentences.en: and that fertile estuary environment was filled with all kinds of marine life.
sentences.zh: 那个肥沃的河口环境里充满了各种海洋生物。

sentences.en: But one majestic creature in particular shaped the landscape.
sentences.zh: 但有一种雄伟的生物特别塑造了这里的景观。

sentences.en: It's estimated probably in the trillions of oysters surrounded New York City.
sentences.zh: 据估计，纽约市周围可能有数万亿只牡蛎。

sentences.en: Before European colonization, what we now think of as the New York City harbor was a veritable oyster kingdom.
sentences.zh: 在欧洲殖民之前，我们现在认为的纽约港是一个名副其实的牡蛎王国。

sentences.en: Some scientists think it contained nearly half the world's oysters.
sentences.zh: 一些科学家认为它包含了世界上近一半的牡蛎。

sentences.en: And they were an important part of the ecosystem.
sentences.zh: 它们是生态系统的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: Oysters are filter feeders, and they help keep bacteria levels in check.
sentences.zh: 牡蛎是滤食性动物，它们有助于控制细菌水平。

sentences.en: In addition to their ability to filter the water, oysters did a huge amount to buffer the city against storm surges.
sentences.zh: 除了过滤水的能力外，牡蛎在缓冲城市免受风暴潮影响方面也发挥了巨大作用。

sentences.en: Because oysters are kind of special.
sentences.zh: 因为牡蛎有点特别。

sentences.en: They are unique among mollusks in that they build in three dimensions.
sentences.zh: 它们在软体动物中是独一无二的，因为它们是三维生长的。

sentences.en: So they're really architects in a sense.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，它们确实是建筑师。

sentences.en: Oysters like to grow on top of other oysters.
sentences.zh: 牡蛎喜欢在其他牡蛎上面生长。

sentences.en: They actually sense the chemical basicness of oyster shell,
sentences.zh: 它们实际上能感知到牡蛎壳的化学碱性，

sentences.en: and they will seed directly on top of other oysters.
sentences.zh: 并会直接在其他牡蛎上面播种。

sentences.en: So you get these aggregations, these clumps that build, build, build, and build.
sentences.zh: 所以你会得到这些聚集体，这些不断生长、生长、再生长的团块。

sentences.en: And eventually they build up into massive, complex reef structures, kind of like coral reefs.
sentences.zh: 最终它们长成了巨大的、复杂的礁石结构，有点像珊瑚礁。

sentences.en: Well, oysters really are the coral reefs of temperate zones.
sentences.zh: 嗯，牡蛎确实是温带地区的珊瑚礁。

sentences.en: Oyster reefs covered over 220,000 acres in the Hudson River estuary.
sentences.zh: 牡蛎礁覆盖了哈德逊河口超过22万英亩的土地。

sentences.en: And sometimes they grew as high as 20 feet tall.
sentences.zh: 有时它们长得高达20英尺。

sentences.en: Like coral reefs, they cut down on coastal erosion, and were home to all different kinds of fish.
sentences.zh: 像珊瑚礁一样，它们减少了海岸侵蚀，是各种鱼类的家园。

sentences.en: And just as coral reefs helped protect many tropical islands from hurricanes, oysters protected New York City.
sentences.zh: 正如珊瑚礁帮助保护许多热带岛屿免受飓风袭击一样，牡蛎也保护了纽约市。

sentences.en: They broke up large waves before they could crash onto the shore.
sentences.zh: 它们在海浪冲上岸之前就将其打碎了。

sentences.en: And below the surface, their rough texture would increase friction and slow down the water.
sentences.zh: 在水面之下，它们粗糙的纹理会增加摩擦力并减缓水流。

sentences.en: And so an oyster reef spread out over many miles will actually sap the wave energy of waves passing over it.
sentences.zh: 因此，分布在许多英里的牡蛎礁实际上会消耗流经其上的海浪能量。

sentences.en: Most people don't associate New York City with oysters today.
sentences.zh: 今天大多数人不会把纽约市和牡蛎联系在一起。

sentences.en: But back in the 1700s, they were what New York was known for.
sentences.zh: 但在18世纪，它们是纽约的代名词。

sentences.en: Oysters were absolutely central to the identity of New York.
sentences.zh: 牡蛎对纽约的身份绝对至关重要。

sentences.en: You know, if somebody were to say, I'm going to New York, they would say, enjoy the oysters.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果有人说，我要去纽约，他们会说，好好享受牡蛎吧。

sentences.en: This is Mark Kurlansky, author of many books, including an environmental history of New York City called The Big Oyster.
sentences.zh: 这是马克·库兰斯基，他著有多本书，包括一本关于纽约市的环境史《大牡蛎》。

sentences.en: Kurlansky says that before colonization, the indigenous Lenape people ate lots of oysters.
sentences.zh: 库兰斯基说，在殖民之前，土著莱纳佩人吃了很多牡蛎。

sentences.en: And when the Dutch arrived in the area, they found an oyster paradise.
sentences.zh: 当荷兰人到达该地区时，他们发现了一个牡蛎天堂。

sentences.en: You know, you could just walk down to the shore anywhere, certainly in lower Manhattan where everybody was living,
sentences.zh: 你知道，你可以随便走到任何地方的岸边，当然是在每个人都居住的曼哈顿下城，

sentences.en: but anywhere, and, you know, break off a few oysters to eat.
sentences.zh: 但在任何地方，你都可以掰下几个牡蛎来吃。

sentences.en: And that's exactly what they did.
sentences.zh: 而这正是他们所做的。

sentences.en: Everybody in New York ate oysters.
sentences.zh: 纽约的每个人都吃牡蛎。

sentences.en: It was said that the only thing that poor people ever got to eat was oysters and bread.
sentences.zh: 据说穷人唯一能吃的东西就是牡蛎和面包。

sentences.en: But it was also something that rich people ate.
sentences.zh: 但这也是富人吃的东西。

sentences.en: Kind of unusual in food history to have a rich people food and a poor people food be the same at the same time.
sentences.zh: 在食物史上，富人的食物和穷人的食物在同一时间是同一种东西，这有点不寻常。

sentences.en: Oysters were sold in street carts and bars, but also fancy restaurants.
sentences.zh: 牡蛎在街头小贩和酒吧里出售，也出现在高级餐厅里。

sentences.en: And they were served in all different kinds of ways.
sentences.zh: 它们以各种不同的方式供应。

sentences.en: Oh, well, there were lots of things.
sentences.zh: 哦，嗯，有很多种。

sentences.en: There were like oyster loaves and oysters with different kinds of sauces, and there were oyster stews.
sentences.zh: 有牡蛎面包、配有各种酱汁的牡蛎，还有牡蛎炖汤。

sentences.en: Discarded oyster shells piled up in huge mounds outside of shucking houses and restaurants.
sentences.zh: 丢弃的牡蛎壳在剥壳房和餐馆外堆成了巨大的土堆。

sentences.en: They were so plentiful that builders began using oysters as construction material.
sentences.zh: 它们非常丰富，以至于建筑商开始把牡蛎当作建筑材料。

sentences.en: Shells were burned to create lime, ground up for mortar, or used to pave streets.
sentences.zh: 贝壳被烧制成石灰，磨碎用于砂浆，或用于铺路。

sentences.en: For instance, Pearl Street in Lower Manhattan is called Pearl Street because it was originally paved with crushed oyster shells.
sentences.zh: 例如，曼哈顿下城的珍珠街之所以叫珍珠街，是因为它最初是用碎牡蛎壳铺成的。

sentences.en: The demand for oysters was so great that it eventually outstripped New York's bountiful supply.
sentences.zh: 对牡蛎的需求如此之大，以至于最终超过了纽约丰富的供应量。

sentences.en: The Erie Canal and the railroad opened up new markets.
sentences.zh: 伊利运河和铁路开辟了新的市场。

sentences.en: Well, nature could not produce enough oysters for, you know, all the places.
sentences.zh: 嗯，大自然无法为所有地方生产足够的牡蛎。

sentences.en: Once they were shipping them to a lot of places, it was more than the natural beds could provide.
sentences.zh: 一旦它们被运往很多地方，就超过了天然河床所能提供的数量。

sentences.en: By the mid-1800s, New York's natural oyster population had been depleted.
sentences.zh: 到19世纪中叶，纽约的天然牡蛎种群已经枯竭。

sentences.en: Humans had nearly eaten the city's protective shellfish barrier out of existence.
sentences.zh: 人类几乎把这座城市的保护性贝类屏障吃光了。

sentences.en: But that wasn't the end of oysters in New York.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是纽约牡蛎的终结。

sentences.en: When they started to run out of oysters in New York City, they went and got seed from the Chesapeake Bay.
sentences.zh: 当纽约市的牡蛎开始用完时，他们就去切萨皮克湾弄来了种子。

sentences.en: And they planted these baby oysters on long ropes strung in rows throughout the shallows of the harbor.
sentences.zh: 他们把这些幼小的牡蛎种在长绳上，成排地挂在港口的浅滩中。

sentences.en: Farming oysters works quite well.
sentences.zh: 养殖牡蛎效果很好。

sentences.en: And it was kind of the next logical step.
sentences.zh: 这算是下一个合乎逻辑的步骤。

sentences.en: You know, if you need more oysters than grow there with nature, you just grow some yourself.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你需要的牡蛎比自然生长的多，你就自己种一些。

sentences.en: Oyster farming continued throughout the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 牡蛎养殖在整个19世纪持续进行。

sentences.en: And by the 1880s, the city was producing over 700 million oysters per year.
sentences.zh: 到19世纪80年代，该市每年生产超过7亿只牡蛎。

sentences.en: But there was a problem lurking in the water.
sentences.zh: 但水里潜伏着一个问题。

sentences.en: For years, the city had been dumping industrial pollutants and sewage straight into the harbor without a second thought.
sentences.zh: 多年来，该市一直不假思索地将工业污染物和污水直接倾倒进港口。

sentences.en: It didn't seem to register with people that dumping raw sewage on a food supply would be unhealthy.
sentences.zh: 人们似乎没有意识到，将未经处理的污水倾倒在食物供应源上是不健康的。

sentences.en: It seemed sort of intuitive to me, but they didn't really, they didn't worry about that.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说似乎是直觉，但他们并没有真正担心过这个问题。

sentences.en: That is, until the early 1900s, when New York was hit with deadly outbreaks of cholera and typhoid.
sentences.zh: 直到20世纪初，纽约爆发了致命的霍乱和伤寒。

sentences.en: And public health officials were able to track the diseases back to the source.
sentences.zh: 公共卫生官员能够追踪到这些疾病的源头。

sentences.en: Turned out that most of these epidemics were coming from oyster beds.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这些流行病大多来自牡蛎床。

sentences.en: And so, one by one, the city started shutting down the oyster beds.
sentences.zh: 于是，该市开始一个接一个地关闭牡蛎床。

sentences.en: Which was really upsetting for New Yorkers.
sentences.zh: 这对纽约人来说真的很令人沮丧。

sentences.en: It was huge front page news every time they closed an oyster bed.
sentences.zh: 每次关闭牡蛎床都是头版头条的大新闻。

sentences.en: And there'd be all these articles about how we have to do something about this.
sentences.zh: 会有各种文章讨论我们必须为此做点什么。

sentences.en: We're losing our heritage, we're losing our oysters, and we have to stop this.
sentences.zh: 我们正在失去我们的遗产，我们正在失去我们的牡蛎，我们必须停止这一切。

sentences.en: But they somehow didn't get it stopped.
sentences.zh: 但他们不知何故没能阻止它。

sentences.en: New York closed its last remaining oyster bed off the south coast of Staten Island in 1927.
sentences.zh: 纽约于1927年关闭了位于斯塔滕岛南岸的最后一个牡蛎床。

sentences.en: Water quality continued to deteriorate until oysters could no longer survive.
sentences.zh: 水质持续恶化，直到牡蛎无法再存活。

sentences.en: The water was so acidic, it would actually etch through the shells.
sentences.zh: 水太酸了，甚至会腐蚀贝壳。

sentences.en: By the middle of the 20th century, New York's world-famous oysters were all but gone.
sentences.zh: 到20世纪中叶，纽约世界闻名的牡蛎几乎消失殆尽。

sentences.en: Leaving the sea bottom barren and the city exposed.
sentences.zh: 使海底变得贫瘠，城市也暴露在外。

sentences.en: Pollution continues to be a problem in New York.
sentences.zh: 污染仍然是纽约的一个问题。

sentences.en: But in 1972, Congress passed the Clean Water Act, which regulated the waste being dumped into waterways.
sentences.zh: 但在1972年，国会通过了《清洁水法》，规范了倾倒在水道中的废物。

sentences.en: And little by little, water quality in the harbor has improved.
sentences.zh: 一点一点地，港口的水质得到了改善。

sentences.en: Now, oxygen levels are high enough to support shellfish, so theoretically, we could have shellfish again throughout the bay.
sentences.zh: 现在，氧气水平足以支持贝类生存，所以理论上，我们可以在整个海湾再次拥有贝类。

sentences.en: This is Paul Greenberg again.
sentences.zh: 这是保罗·格林伯格。

sentences.en: In his book, American Catch, he documents several different groups who are working really hard to try and bring back the New York oyster.
sentences.zh: 在他的书《美国渔获》中，他记录了几个正在努力尝试带回纽约牡蛎的团体。

sentences.en: There are a lot of obstacles in their way, including FDA rules, which make it really hard to plant oysters.
sentences.zh: 他们面临着许多障碍，包括FDA的规定，这使得种植牡蛎变得非常困难。

sentences.en: And the fact that there just isn't enough wild oyster larvae in the water anymore.
sentences.zh: 而且水里确实不再有足够的野生牡蛎幼虫了。

sentences.en: But one of the biggest challenges is actually an architectural one.
sentences.zh: 但最大的挑战之一实际上是建筑方面的。

sentences.en: Because the physical landscape of the harbor has totally changed.
sentences.zh: 因为港口的物理景观已经完全改变了。

sentences.en: We've been dredging the harbor for over 150 years now.
sentences.zh: 我们疏浚港口已经超过150年了。

sentences.en: It went from an average depth of 20 feet to places where now it's more than 50 feet.
sentences.zh: 平均水深从20英尺增加到了现在有些地方超过50英尺。

sentences.en: And the bottom looks very different.
sentences.zh: 而且海底看起来也大不相同了。

sentences.en: Right now, our harbor has a flat, muddy bottom.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们的港口底部是平坦的泥地。

sentences.en: But, you know, if we were to look at, say, 1850, 1880, this would have been an extremely kind of rougher three-dimensional mosaic.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，如果我们看看1850年或1880年，那时的海底会是一种极其粗糙的三维马赛克状结构。

sentences.en: This is Kate Orff.
sentences.zh: 这位是凯特·奥夫（Kate Orff）。

sentences.en: She's a landscape architect and founder of the firm Scape, based in Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 她是一位景观设计师，也是位于曼哈顿的Scape事务所的创始人。

sentences.en: And she's the author of the new book, Towards an Urban Ecology.
sentences.zh: 她还是新书《迈向城市生态》（Towards an Urban Ecology）的作者。

sentences.en: She also just became the first landscape architect to win a MacArthur Genius Award.
sentences.zh: 她最近还成为了第一位获得麦克阿瑟天才奖的景观设计师。

sentences.en: And Orff says that a flat, muddy bottom just does not work well for oysters.
sentences.zh: 奥夫说，平坦的泥泞海底对牡蛎来说并不友好。

sentences.en: There are no places or very few places for oysters to grab onto and to attach.
sentences.zh: 那里几乎没有可以让牡蛎抓附的地方。

sentences.en: Right now, there are some oyster larvae floating around out there.
sentences.zh: 现在，海里确实漂浮着一些牡蛎幼虫。

sentences.en: But they don't really stand a chance.
sentences.zh: 但它们几乎没有生存机会。

sentences.en: Any oyster that lands on the bottom of the bay's bed will then immediately be covered with silt.
sentences.zh: 任何落到海湾底部的牡蛎都会立刻被淤泥覆盖。

sentences.en: So we need to lift those oysters off of the bay floor.
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要把这些牡蛎从海床上抬升起来。

sentences.en: And we need to provide substrate for these creatures to attach onto.
sentences.zh: 我们需要为这些生物提供可以附着的基质。

sentences.en: That challenge gave Orff an idea that spawned one of my favorite portmanteaus, oyster texture.
sentences.zh: 这个挑战给了奥夫一个灵感，催生了我最喜欢的合成词之一：牡蛎纹理（oyster texture）。

sentences.en: The concept was to build giant nets made of fuzzy marine rope and elevate them off the seafloor.
sentences.zh: 这个概念是用模糊的海洋绳索制作巨大的网，并将它们从海床上抬高。

sentences.en: They would then seed the nets with oyster larvae and let the oysters grow from there.
sentences.zh: 然后他们在网上播撒牡蛎幼虫，让牡蛎在那里生长。

sentences.en: So it agglomerates in the sense of becoming a megastructure that scales up out of very small organisMs.
sentences.zh: 它通过这种方式聚集，形成了一种由微小生物扩展而成的巨型结构。

sentences.en: With a relatively small architectural intervention, you could have a new piece of protective infrastructure, an artificial oyster reef.
sentences.zh: 通过相对较小的建筑干预，你可以拥有一种新的防护基础设施，即人工牡蛎礁。

sentences.en: Which in turn would filter the water, slow the water, and create a safer relationship with that water.
sentences.zh: 这反过来可以过滤水质、减缓水流，并与水体建立更安全的关系。

sentences.en: Kate Orff debuted her oyster texture proposal in 2010 as part of an exhibit at the Museum of Modern Art called Rising Currents.
sentences.zh: 凯特·奥夫在2010年现代艺术博物馆举办的名为“上升的潮流”（Rising Currents）的展览中首次提出了她的“牡蛎纹理”方案。

sentences.en: And it was a speculative project that sparked a ton of conversation.
sentences.zh: 这是一个引发了大量讨论的推测性项目。

sentences.en: But it was never actually built.
sentences.zh: 但它实际上从未被建造出来。

sentences.en: But Hurricane Sandy brought new attention to sea level rise and opened new funding avenues for coastal resilience projects.
sentences.zh: 不过飓风“桑迪”让人们重新关注海平面上升，并为海岸韧性项目开辟了新的资金渠道。

sentences.en: In 2013, the federal government launched its Hurricane Sandy Rebuilding Task Force and staged an architectural competition called Rebuild by Design.
sentences.zh: 2013年，联邦政府成立了“飓风桑迪重建特别工作组”，并举办了一场名为“重建设计”（Rebuild by Design）的建筑竞赛。

sentences.en: SCAPE, that's Kate Orff's architecture firm, submitted an oyster-centric proposal called Living Breakwaters.
sentences.zh: SCAPE，也就是凯特·奥夫的建筑事务所，提交了一份以牡蛎为核心的方案，名为“生命防波堤”（Living Breakwaters）。

sentences.en: The project receives $60 million of funding and will be carried out by the Governor's Office of Storm Recovery.
sentences.zh: 该项目获得了6000万美元的资金，并将由州长风暴恢复办公室负责实施。

sentences.en: Now SCAPE is in the process of designing artificial oyster reef breakwaters off the south coast of Staten Island.
sentences.zh: 现在，SCAPE正在斯塔滕岛南岸设计人工牡蛎礁防波堤。

sentences.en: Staten Island was particularly hard hit by Hurricane Sandy.
sentences.zh: 斯塔滕岛在飓风“桑迪”中受灾尤为严重。

sentences.en: This is Gina Wirth, another one of the architects from SCAPE, explaining the choice of location.
sentences.zh: 这位是吉娜·沃斯（Gina Wirth），SCAPE的另一位建筑师，她解释了选址的原因。

sentences.en: And the wave action from the surge landed right on Staten Island and really dramatically impacted this landmass.
sentences.zh: 风暴潮带来的波浪直接冲击斯塔滕岛，对这片陆地造成了巨大的影响。

sentences.en: Staten Island was also one of the epicenters of New York's historic oyster economy.
sentences.zh: 斯塔滕岛也是纽约历史上牡蛎经济的中心之一。

sentences.en: So it's not the first time that people have been trying to cultivate and expand oysters within the bay.
sentences.zh: 所以，这并不是人们第一次尝试在海湾内培育和扩大牡蛎种群。

sentences.en: You know, hundreds of years ago they were doing it for food production, and today we're trying to do it for a more robust and resilient shoreline.
sentences.zh: 你知道，几百年前他们这样做是为了生产食物，而今天我们这样做是为了拥有更稳固、更具韧性的海岸线。

sentences.en: The design has evolved a lot from the original oyster texture proposal with the marine rope.
sentences.zh: 现在的设计与最初使用海洋绳索的“牡蛎纹理”方案相比已经有了很大演变。

sentences.en: The plan now is to build a necklace of offshore breakwaters out of large rocks and a special material called eco-concrete, which shellfish like to grow on.
sentences.zh: 现在的计划是用大石头和一种贝类喜欢生长的特殊材料——生态混凝土，建造一串近海防波堤。

sentences.en: They will then seed the breakwaters with oysters, so they grow into reefs.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会在防波堤上播撒牡蛎，让它们长成礁石。

sentences.en: Much like a natural oyster reef, the living breakwaters are designed to slow down the water and break up dangerous waves before they reach the shore.
sentences.zh: 就像天然牡蛎礁一样，这些生命防波堤旨在减缓水流，并在危险波浪到达岸边前将其打散。

sentences.en: So as the oysters grow, they really help add friction to the water column and break waves.
sentences.zh: 随着牡蛎的生长，它们确实有助于增加水柱的摩擦力并破碎波浪。

sentences.en: The living breakwaters should reduce coastal erosion, build up beaches, and make storms less dangerous.
sentences.zh: 生命防波堤应该能减少海岸侵蚀、堆积沙滩，并降低风暴的危险性。

sentences.en: Modeling by scientists at the Stevens Institute has shown that the breakwaters could have reduced the height of waves during Sandy by three to six feet.
sentences.zh: 史蒂文斯理工学院科学家的模型显示，在“桑迪”飓风期间，这些防波堤本可以将波高降低三到六英尺。

sentences.en: But they won't keep floodwater out of Staten Island altogether, and they're not meant to.
sentences.zh: 但它们并不能完全将洪水挡在斯塔滕岛之外，它们的设计初衷也不是为了这个。

sentences.en: The breakwaters let the water through.
sentences.zh: 防波堤允许水流通过。

sentences.en: We can reduce the wave action.
sentences.zh: 我们可以减少波浪作用。

sentences.en: We can reduce the intensity and the velocity of that water.
sentences.zh: 我们可以降低水流的强度和速度。

sentences.en: But we live on a coastal edge.
sentences.zh: 但我们生活在海岸边缘。

sentences.en: And Worth wants to design a way to make that coastal edge safer and healthier, both for humans and for marine life.
sentences.zh: 沃斯希望设计一种方法，让这个海岸边缘对人类和海洋生物来说都更安全、更健康。

sentences.en: In addition to reducing waves and filtering the water, the living breakwaters will provide some of the habitat that oyster reefs once did.
sentences.zh: 除了减少波浪和过滤水质外，生命防波堤还将提供一些牡蛎礁曾经提供的栖息地。

sentences.en: Staten Island's historic oyster reefs were filled with all these nooks and crannies where juvenile fish liked to hide.
sentences.zh: 斯塔滕岛历史上的牡蛎礁充满了各种小鱼喜欢躲藏的缝隙和角落。

sentences.en: With the help of marine biologists, the architects designed pockets within the breakwater structure.
sentences.zh: 在海洋生物学家的帮助下，建筑师们在防波堤结构中设计了口袋空间。

sentences.en: They call them reef streets.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为“礁石街道”。

sentences.en: So within the reef streets, a juvenile fish are able to come into these kind of underwater canyons and feed in the street and shelter and hide from predators in the structure.
sentences.zh: 在这些礁石街道里，幼鱼可以进入这些水下峡谷，在街道中觅食，并在结构中躲避捕食者。

sentences.en: Worth says that as a landscape architect, your clients are usually people.
sentences.zh: 沃斯说，作为一名景观设计师，你的客户通常是人。

sentences.en: But we're also trying to think about who are our underwater clients, who are the fish species that might use this system.
sentences.zh: 但我们也在思考谁是我们的水下客户，即哪些鱼类可能会使用这个系统。

sentences.en: Like if you were a fish swimming in the water, what would look like a safe place?
sentences.zh: 比如，如果你是一条在水里游的鱼，什么地方看起来像个安全的地方？

sentences.en: It's like a totally different mentality to have when designing than what a person looks for.
sentences.zh: 这与人类寻找的设计视角完全不同。

sentences.en: Construction hasn't begun yet on the physical structure of the breakwater.
sentences.zh: 防波堤的物理结构建设尚未开始。

sentences.en: But some of the oysters are already growing.
sentences.zh: 但一些牡蛎已经在生长了。

sentences.en: Oysters growing over here.
sentences.zh: 牡蛎正在这边生长。

sentences.en: This is Asia Salgado, a recent graduate of the New York Harbor School on Governor's Island.
sentences.zh: 这位是亚洲·萨尔加多（Asia Salgado），她是总督岛纽约港口学校的应届毕业生。

sentences.en: All these guys right here?
sentences.zh: 所有这些家伙都在这儿吗？

sentences.en: The Harbor School runs a program called the Billion Oyster Project, which aims to restore oysters throughout the harbor.
sentences.zh: 港口学校运营着一个名为“十亿牡蛎项目”（Billion Oyster Project）的项目，旨在恢复整个港口的牡蛎。

sentences.en: And in the process, teach young New Yorkers all about the marine ecosystem.
sentences.zh: 并在此过程中，向年轻的纽约人传授有关海洋生态系统的知识。

sentences.en: Asia is standing next to a tank filled with white shells soaking in harbor water.
sentences.zh: 亚洲正站在一个装满浸泡在港口水中的白色贝壳的水箱旁。

sentences.en: There are actually leftover shells from restaurants.
sentences.zh: 这些其实是餐馆剩下的贝壳。

sentences.en: So we'll go around and we'll collect shell from different restaurants around the city.
sentences.zh: 我们会四处收集城市里不同餐馆的贝壳。

sentences.en: And on the surface of every shell, there are little oysters growing.
sentences.zh: 在每个贝壳的表面，都有小牡蛎在生长。

sentences.en: You see all these big brown dots over here?
sentences.zh: 你看到这边所有这些大的棕色斑点了吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Those are all oysters.
sentences.zh: 那些都是牡蛎。

sentences.en: They look like little blobs of brown jelly.
sentences.zh: 它们看起来像一小团棕色的果冻。

sentences.en: But if you get really close, you can see the beginnings of an oyster.
sentences.zh: 但如果你凑近看，就能看到牡蛎的雏形。

sentences.en: You can kind of tell on this one.
sentences.zh: 在这个上你能看出来。

sentences.en: This one has like stripes on it.
sentences.zh: 这个上面有条纹。

sentences.en: That's how you know that's like its own shell slowly growing.
sentences.zh: 这就是你怎么知道那是它自己正在缓慢生长的外壳。

sentences.en: Once it gets bigger, obviously it'll look like one of these shells.
sentences.zh: 一旦它长大了，显然它看起来就会像这些贝壳一样。

sentences.en: But it's getting there slowly.
sentences.zh: 但它正在慢慢长大。

sentences.en: The Billion Oyster Project is an official partner on the Living Breakwaters,
sentences.zh: “十亿牡蛎项目”是“生命防波堤”的官方合作伙伴，

sentences.en: meaning that millions of little brown balls of goo grown by young New Yorkers like Asia
sentences.zh: 这意味着由像亚洲这样的年轻纽约人培育的数百万个棕色小粘球，

sentences.en: will soon be protecting Staten Island.
sentences.zh: 很快就会开始保护斯塔滕岛。

sentences.en: The Governor's Office of Storm Recovery is scheduled to begin construction of the Living Breakwaters in 2018.
sentences.zh: 州长风暴恢复办公室计划于2018年开始建设“生命防波堤”。

sentences.en: The Billion Oyster Project will work with local high schools on Staten Island to monitor oyster growth over time.
sentences.zh: “十亿牡蛎项目”将与斯塔滕岛当地的高中合作，监测牡蛎随时间的生长情况。

sentences.en: A healthy reef can grow very quickly, so we're very optimistic that by, say, 2025,
sentences.zh: 健康的礁石生长非常迅速，所以我们非常乐观，比如到2025年，

sentences.en: we would have a pretty robust reef system going.
sentences.zh: 我们就能拥有一个相当稳健的礁石系统。

sentences.en: Kate Orff says that even if they're successful,
sentences.zh: 凯特·奥夫说，即使他们成功了，

sentences.en: they aren't going to return the coastal environment to the way it was before.
sentences.zh: 他们也无法将沿海环境恢复到以前的样子。

sentences.en: No architect can do that.
sentences.zh: 没有建筑师能做到这一点。

sentences.en: They're creating something totally new.
sentences.zh: 他们正在创造一些全新的东西。

sentences.en: Part ecosystem, part infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 既是生态系统，也是基础设施。

sentences.en: And Orff hopes that they inspire other living infrastructure projects.
sentences.zh: 奥夫希望它们能激发其他生命基础设施项目。

sentences.en: But she doesn't think that oysters are going to save New York from climate change.
sentences.zh: 但她并不认为牡蛎能拯救纽约免受气候变化的影响。

sentences.en: There isn't any one solution to a problem so immense and complex.
sentences.zh: 对于如此巨大且复杂的问题，没有任何单一的解决方案。

sentences.en: Researchers at the organization Climate Central recently ranked New York
sentences.zh: 气候中心（Climate Central）组织的科研人员最近将纽约列为

sentences.en: as the most vulnerable city in the United States to sea level rise,
sentences.zh: 美国受海平面上升影响最脆弱的城市，

sentences.en: with over 426,000 people living in zones that could face serious flooding by 2050.
sentences.zh: 到2050年，有超过42.6万人居住在可能面临严重洪水的区域。

sentences.en: When you start projecting out further than 2050,
sentences.zh: 当你开始预测2050年以后的情况时，

sentences.en: the scale of the problem becomes hard to fathom.
sentences.zh: 问题的规模就变得难以想象了。

sentences.en: I mean, it's really hard, frankly, to be optimistic.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，坦率地说，真的很难保持乐观。

sentences.en: We're on track for a pretty rapid sea level rise.
sentences.zh: 我们正处于海平面快速上升的轨道上。

sentences.en: And, you know, can we kind of come together and proactively see this as an urban design opportunity
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们能否团结起来，主动地将其视为一个城市设计的机会，

sentences.en: and not a force that just displaces thousands of people with less economic means
sentences.zh: 而不是一种只会让成千上万经济条件较差、

sentences.en: and who are less fortunate?
sentences.zh: 不太幸运的人流离失所的力量？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I think it's going to be a real challenge.
sentences.zh: 我认为这将是一个真正的挑战。

sentences.en: Orff sees the Living Breakwaters project as a step toward a healthier relationship
sentences.zh: 奥夫将“生命防波堤”项目视为迈向城市与海洋之间更健康关系的一步。

sentences.en: between the city and the sea.
sentences.zh: 但为了从长远保护纽约和其他沿海城市，

sentences.en: But to protect New York and other coastal cities in the long term,
sentences.zh: 还有许多其他干预措施需要考虑。

sentences.en: there are going to be a lot of other interventions that will need to be considered.
sentences.zh: 停止在海岸进行新开发，抬高现有建筑，

sentences.en: Ending new development on coasts, lifting existing buildings up,
sentences.zh: 最终，在某些地方，

sentences.en: and eventually, in some places,
sentences.zh: 从易受洪水侵袭的地区撤离。

sentences.en: Retreating, literally, from flood-prone areas.
sentences.zh: 我们能进行那些艰难的对话吗？

sentences.en: And can we have those hard conversations?
sentences.zh: 我当然希望如此。

sentences.en: I certainly hope so.
sentences.zh: 我也希望如此。
